intro.text: 今天的 feed 有一条很清楚的主线：AI builder 们正在把注意力从“模型能不能做”转向“怎样把它做得更快、更可靠、更像真正的工作流”。Stefano Ermon 把 diffusion 推理的优势归结为并行性和单位成本；Guillermo Rauch 则提醒，低质量的 AI prose 正在消耗人们阅读和理解的耐心。另一边，Thariq 记录了 Claude Code 做视频从“要反复调很久”到一年后明显变快的距离，Peter Yang 直接用 Gemini audio API 做了一个日语学习 app。

sections.title: Inference Is the Product / 推理本身就是产品
sections.desc: 当模型质量越来越接近，速度、并行性和单位成本开始决定真实体验。

rewrite: Stefano Ermon, the Stanford professor who co-founded Inception, is betting that diffusion models can challenge autoregressive LLMs where it matters most: inference. His argument is straightforward: autoregressive generation is still sequential and memory-bound, while diffusion can process many tokens in parallel and map better to GPUs.

That makes speed more than a benchmark metric. It changes voice agents, rollouts for RL post-training, and the economics of serving intelligence. Ermon's company is now building its own serving engine for diffusion-based language models, because the existing LLM stack was designed around a different generation pattern.
original: Autoregressive models are still sequential at inference time. You cannot generate the tenth token until you've generated everything that comes before it, and that workload does not map well to GPUs.
A diffusion model is built to have, at inference time, a workload where you process many tokens at the same time.

rewrite: Stefano Ermon 是 Stanford 教授，也是 Inception 的联合创始人。他押注 diffusion model 会在最重要的地方挑战 autoregressive LLM：推理。理由很直接：autoregressive 生成仍然是串行的、受内存带宽限制，而 diffusion 可以并行处理多个 token，更适合 GPU。
所以速度不只是 benchmark 指标，它会改变 voice agent、RL post-training 的 rollout，以及部署 intelligence 的成本结构。Inception 甚至在自己做 diffusion language model 的 serving engine，因为现有 LLM 基础设施原本就是为另一种生成方式设计的。
original: Autoregressive 模型在推理时仍然是串行的，必须先生成前面的 token，才能生成第十个 token，这种工作负载并不适合 GPU。
Diffusion model 在推理时可以同时处理多个 token。

rewrite: Peter Yang is building a small but telling app with the Gemini audio API: ten conversational-Japanese lessons, ten phrases per lesson. The interesting part is not the size of the app; it is how quickly a personal learning loop can now be assembled around a multimodal API.
original: Building an app with Gemini audio API to teach me conversational Japanese. 10 lessons and 10 phrases per lesson.

rewrite: Peter Yang 正在用 Gemini audio API 做一个很小、但很有代表性的 app：10 节会话日语课，每节 10 个短语。重点不在 app 有多大，而在于现在已经可以围绕一个 multimodal API，很快搭出属于自己的学习闭环。
original: 用 Gemini audio API 做一个教我会话日语的 app：10 节课，每节 10 个短语。

rewrite: Ermon also makes a useful case for why academic research still matters in an era of enormous compute budgets. Diffusion models, FlashAttention, and DPO all began with ideas developed in academic settings, where researchers can afford to take contrarian bets before the market agrees with them. The lesson is not that academia has enough resources; it is that a clever insight can still open a new path.
original: One of the nice things about academia is that it allows you to take these contrarian bets.
There are gems, there are lots of opportunities for finding new and better ways of solving important problems.

rewrite: Ermon 还解释了为什么在 compute 预算巨大的时代，学术研究依然重要。Diffusion model、FlashAttention 和 DPO 都起源于学术环境里的想法，在那里研究者可以先押注一个反共识方向，不必等市场先证明它。重点不是学术界资源充足，而是一个聪明的 insight 仍然可能打开一条新路。
original: 学术界的一个好处是，它允许你做这些反共识的押注。
还有很多宝藏，很多机会，可以用新的、更好的方式解决重要问题。

sections.title: From Demo to Workflow / 从 demo 到工作流
sections.desc: 真正的变化不是模型第一次做出来，而是同一件事一年后要少花多少力气。

rewrite: Thariq looks back at one of his first posts about using Claude Code to make videos. A year ago, each result took a long time to iterate on, with careful corrections for all the details that were wrong. His short update is a useful measure of progress: the workflow has become dramatically easier to push toward a good result.
original: Just about 1 year ago I posted one of the first posts about using Claude Code to make videos. Each of these actually took a long time to iterate with Claude and get right, pointing out details that were wrong, etc. Crazy how far things have come.

rewrite: Thariq 回看了一年前自己最早用 Claude Code 做视频的帖子。那时每个结果都要花很久反复迭代，还要一点点指出错误的细节。这个短更新提供了一个很好的进步尺度：真正变快的不是 demo，而是把结果推向“能用”的整个工作流。
original: 大约一年前，我发了最早一批用 Claude Code 做视频的帖子。每一个都要花很久和 Claude 反复迭代，指出错误的细节。变化真的太大了。

rewrite: Garry Tan shares a concrete production workflow he now likes for fixing bugs: run Capi with GStack's /autoplan on the issue, using GPT-6 medium reasoning. The point is not a grand theory of agents; it is a specific handoff from a production problem to a precise bug spec.
original: This is my favorite way to fix bugs now @capydotai with GStack /autoplan on a production issue GPT-6 medium reasoning

rewrite: Garry Tan 分享了他现在喜欢的一套生产环境修 bug 流程：在 production issue 上用 Capi 跑 GStack 的 /autoplan，并使用 GPT-6 medium reasoning。重点不是又一个宏大的 agent 理论，而是把真实问题交给 agent，直接产出更精确的 bug spec。
original: 我现在最喜欢的修 bug 方式：在 production issue 上用 Capi + GStack /autoplan，GPT-6 medium reasoning。

sections.title: The Cost of Slop / Slop 的代价
sections.desc: AI 生成内容的价值不只取决于产出速度，也取决于它有没有帮助人理解问题。

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch argues that AI slop is putting reading itself at risk. The problem is not limited to bad code or noisy PRs: after enough low-quality, unverified AI prose, people start discounting the act of reading. He points to a performance improvement wrongly attributed to a compiler change, when the real cause was a change in algorithms and data structures.
His standard is simple and demanding: AI should serve understanding of the universe and enhance human cognition and creativity, not make confident explanations cheaper than careful thinking.
original: Slop grenades are not just code and PRs. We run a real risk that reading gets entirely discounted, because of the exhaustion of getting low-quality and unverified AI prose thrown at you all the time.
I want AI in the service of understanding the universe and enhancing human cognition and creativity.

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 认为，AI slop 正在让“阅读”本身变得不被信任。问题不只在糟糕的代码或嘈杂的 PR：当人们长期被低质量、未经验证的 AI prose 轰炸，就会连认真阅读这件事都开始打折。他举了一个例子：一项性能提升被错误归因于 compiler 改动，实际原因却是算法和数据结构变了。
他的标准很简单，也很高：AI 应该服务于理解世界，增强人的认知和创造力，而不是让自信但未经核验的解释变得更便宜。
original: Slop 不只是代码和 PR。低质量、未经验证的 AI prose 不断出现，会让人因为疲惫而完全不再重视阅读。
我希望 AI 服务于理解世界，增强人的认知和创造力。

rewrite: Dan Shipper is testing a different kind of AI-native creative workflow: he wrote a novelization of Plato's Protagoras, then had Opus 5.5 turn it into a short film, sharing a second scene after the first. It is a compact example of a writer moving from text to screen through a model, with the creative source still clearly his own.
original: Plato's Protagoras, as a short film by Opus 5.5. scene 2:
i wrote a novelization of Plato’s Protagoras then i had Opus 5.5 turn it into a movie (scene 1)

rewrite: Dan Shipper 在测试一种 AI-native 的创作流程：先把 Plato 的《Protagoras》写成小说化版本，再让 Opus 5.5 把它变成短片，并连续分享了第二个场景。这是一个很紧凑的例子：作者从文字走向画面，中间的转换交给模型，但创作源头依然清楚地属于作者。
original: 由 Opus 5.5 制作的 Plato's Protagoras 短片，场景 2。
我写了 Plato 的《Protagoras》小说化版本，然后让 Opus 5.5 把它拍成电影（场景 1）。
